dedupe_keys.name: stsrs security threats in smart railway systems simulated dataset

description: STSRS (Security Threats in Smart Railway Systems) is a simulated time-series corpus for cybersecurity and intelligent transport research, presented at the 12th International Conference on Information Systems Security and Privacy (ICISSP 2026) by researchers at the University of Huddersfield. It contains over 10 million synchronised records of interactions between 10 autonomous trains and two control centres in normal and adversarial scenarios (denial of service, jamming and stealthy replay). It was generated with a modular framework using stochastic dynamics, TCP/IP telemetry and context-aware attack injection, and each record has more than 10 labelled features, both raw (such as speed and latency) and behavioural (such as burstiness and entropy). Coverage: a synthetic railway system. Format and access: described in a conference paper. Licence and cost: not stated. Caveats: synthetic, and the paper page does not say where the data are hosted. It supports digital twin evaluation and anomaly detection for railway control communications. It relates to the railway cyber range ICS dataset and the Electra dataset in the catalogue.
